messages.design-accessibility.directory.name: Design and accessibility
messages.design-accessibility.directory.summary: Five Skills for design critique, WCAG 2.1 AA, handoff, design systems and UI copy in Assistant, Coding and Pages.
messages.design-accessibility.skill.accessibility: Review a page, component, design or piece of interface code against WCAG 2.1 AA, and write each finding with where it is, the success criterion it fails, who it affects and how to fix it. Use it when someone asks for an accessibility review, asks whether an interface works with only a keyboard or a screen reader, checks accessibility before a release, or wants to confirm that an interface change introduced no new problems.
There is something concrete to look at (a page, a screenshot, a design, component code or an address that opens), and you want to know how far it is from WCAG 2.1 AA and what to fix first.

You only want an opinion on the overall design (use design-critique); you want interface text written or changed (use ux-copy); you need legal advice or a formal compliance certification, which this review cannot replace.
messages.design-accessibility.skill.design-critiq: Give a structured design critique of an interface, a flow or a design: first learn whom it helps do what, then look for problems in whether the task can be completed, visual hierarchy, consistency, states and feedback, and density, writing for each the evidence, the impact and a concrete fix, and separating what must change from what to consider. Use it when someone asks for a design review, asks what is wrong with a page or prototype, wants to compare options, or wants a changed interface picked apart.

There is something to look at (a screenshot, a design, a prototype, a page that opens or interface code), and you want to know where people will stumble, fail to see or feel lost, and what to fix first.

You only want an accessibility check against WCAG, criterion by criterion (use accessibility-review); you only want text changed (use ux-copy); you want a final design written up for developers to build (use design-handoff); there is no sketch yet, only an idea of what to make.
messages.design-accessibility.skill.design-handof: Turn a settled design into a handoff developers can build from without guessing: scope, every state of each screen, the components and design tokens used, interaction and motion, real text, accessibility requirements, data and edge cases, changes across widths, and open questions; also check what an existing handoff is missing before work starts. Use it when someone writes a design handoff or developer spec, hands a design to developers, or receives a design to implement.
The design is mostly settled and someone else (or Coding) will build it; or you have a design or a handoff and want to know which decisions are still missing before work starts.

The design is still being explored and needs critique first (use design-critique); you only want an accessibility check (use accessibility-review); you only want text changed (use ux-copy); you are maintaining the whole set of components and design tokens (use design-system).
messages.design-accessibility.skill.design-system: Use, extend and audit a design system in code: look for existing design tokens and components before writing interface code; when something new is truly needed, name it by layer, complete its states, themes and accessibility, and add its specimen to the component board; audit a codebase for drift from the design system (hard-coded colours and sizes, one-off components, operating-system controls) and give an order for migrating. Use it when writing or changing interface code, adding a component or design token, or cleaning up interface inconsistencies.

You are writing interface code in a project that has a design system (design tokens, a component library, a component board or a design document); you need to decide between reusing and building new; you want to take stock of and gather up inconsistencies in the interface.

You want to judge whether an interface is easy to use (use design-critique); you want an accessibility check (use accessibility-review); you are writing a handoff for developers (use design-handoff); the project has no design system yet and this is a one-off prototype.
messages.design-accessibility.skill.ux-copy.descr: Write and revise interface text: buttons, headings, empty states, errors, confirmations, notices, loading, permission requests and onboarding. Write to say what happened and what can be done next, keep the same words throughout, follow each language’s own conventions in Chinese and English, and never join half-sentences or force a count into a sentence. Use it when someone writes or revises interface copy, finds a phrase awkward or unclear, wants the words in one feature made consistent, or needs English for interface text.
messages.design-accessibility.skill.ux-copy.when-: There is specific interface text or a specific interface to write for, revise or check, including making a whole flow’s words consistent and pairing Chinese with English.

Writing marketing articles, long help documents or announcements; judging the overall design (use design-critique); checking accessibility (use accessibility-review, which also points out problems with names and error messages).
